checklist.evidence: Actual tenant tables have RLS enabled and forced. The runtime role cannot bypass RLS or act as a superuser. Identity/membership checks bind transaction-local tenant scope. PostgreSQL and API cross-tenant regressions verify rejection.

An inventory test requires owned cookie authentication on every private OpenAPI operation. Public registration/login/recovery/verification/Google-proof initiation, CSRF/config and minimal health endpoints are deliberate exceptions. Refresh authenticates its stored refresh token rather than requiring a still-valid access token. Privileged business actions require server-side membership/permissions and MFA.

Pydantic schemas reject undeclared fields; the API and PostgreSQL enforce permissions, currency precision, balances, dates, period locks, immutability and idempotency. Client-side visibility or totals cannot grant authority.

Auth IP/email, global authenticated user and workspace/user limits use durable shared PostgreSQL counters. Production edge limits for unauthenticated floods and resource-intensive traffic still require proxy/network configuration and load verification. There are no public API keys in current P1.

Use strict type/length/range validation plus context-specific output encoding, not destructive rewriting of financial evidence. React renders text, exports escape HTML and spreadsheet-formula cells, and user input is never treated as executable markup/SQL. The new browser test proves CSP blocks an injected inline script.

SQLAlchemy/bound SQL handle user values. Administrative identifiers are quoted by the database driver's identifier APIs. Transaction rollback and safe database-error envelopes are covered by the preceding database audit.

Origins must be explicit, with no wildcard or URL credentials/path. Methods and headers are bounded. Tests verify allowed and denied preflight; CSRF/Origin checks independently protect writes. CORS is not used as authentication.

Hosted API HTTP requests are rejected before bodies/preflight; HTTPS gets HSTS. Auth cookies are Secure/HttpOnly with explicit SameSite. Hosted PostgreSQL requires verified TLS, and enabled hosted SMTP requires TLS. Private health probes and local same-origin loopback are documented exceptions. Actual certificates, trusted proxy peers, public ingress and Vercel/AWS behavior must be verified in Phase 9/10.

No inbound webhook route exists. This is not marked as a verified webhook implementation. Any future connector must validate raw-body signatures, timestamps/replay, event idempotency and mapped tenant authority before activation; it must not receive a blanket CSRF/auth bypass.

checklist.status: verified for the current product assistant
checklist.evidence: It accepts an allowlisted report metric and returns an authorized report lookup with `actions_executed=false`. It has no arbitrary prompt-to-SQL, shell, migration, payment or posting executor. This refers to the product, not authorized developer tooling used to maintain the repository.

FastAPI debug is false, hosted Swagger/OpenAPI/Redoc routes are unavailable, and errors redact exception/SQL details. Local Swagger has a narrowly documented CSP exception for its existing development assets.

This audit and its tests were performed; no separate Claude service or independent external penetration test was run. A model/vendor label cannot replace the controls or prove absence of vulnerabilities.

checklist.status: local adapter verified; cloud gate pending
checklist.evidence: Current originals are encrypted private files with generated keys, containment checks, restrictive Linux modes, quarantine and authorized attachment-only downloads. There is no cloud bucket to audit yet. Cloud public-access blocking, IAM, encryption/retention policy and deployed volume/host ACLs require actual infrastructure verification before cloud storage is enabled.

No generic execution/admin tool endpoint exists. OCR uses fixed argument arrays, timeouts, a private bearer token and an unprivileged, read-only, resource-limited container without financial credentials or Docker socket. Its ports are loopback-published. Production egress restrictions remain an infrastructure gate; the local Docker Desktop bridge is not claimed to be an outbound firewall.

URL secrecy is not a control. Workspace administration/settings are backed by owned identity, active membership, role/permission and MFA checks. Changing client-side routes or role fields cannot grant administrative access.

Python and web runtime audits now report zero known advisories. Three moderate dev-tool findings remain for one minimatch advisory in the OpenAPI generator chain; see below. Container OS/platform scans and live image promotion remain deployment checks.

API success/rejection/error/CORS responses and production browser script enforcement are tested. The configured Vercel headers still require verification on the deployed hostname. CSP is defense in depth, not a substitute for server validation or safe rendering.

Auth/role checks precede upload buffering; size/type/extension checks and generated storage keys apply. Originals remain quarantined until a positive ClamAV result. Only supported inputs reach bounded OCR; unsupported HEIC/XLSX inputs do not become executable content or unrestricted parsers. Downloads use attachment/octet-stream and nosniff, not inline user HTML.

Membership and tenant/object ownership are checked on the server and reinforced by RLS, including evidence, reports, exports and newly batched queries. Forbidden/unshared records do not become accessible by changing UUIDs. This is regression evidence, not a mathematical guarantee for every future endpoint.

Security/business changes write scoped audit events in the business transaction. Runtime DELETE of audit history is denied. Logs/errors do not contain credentials, tokens or private request bodies. Production collection, alert delivery, retention and incident response still need operational verification.

backend.resolution: The concurrent-registration test assumed every parallel attempt must succeed. The 503 backpressure contract was retained; the test now validates committed issuance counts, controlled completion and the three-issuance/24-hour pause. The updated identity/checklist follow-up passed 25/25. No application admission/hash/lock/rate guards were relaxed. Production logic did not change between the full and focused runs; later main.py changes were formatting only.
